page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a memory-optimized and storage-capable virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB per core, and includes 2880 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities. No GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core results. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is average at 27.93 GB/sec, though read-only memory bandwidth is relatively weak, measuring 303.46 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 36.73 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Cryptographic and text processing tasks perform well, but database operations and software compilation show weaker relative throughput. Large-model LLM inference is highly constrained, though small 135M model inference achieves average speeds of 462.72 tokens/sec for prompt processing.

Given its high local storage capacity of 2880 GB and 32.0 GB of RAM, the L4aos_v4 offers high resource density for storage-heavy and memory-intensive workloads without the premium cost of larger compute-heavy instances. However, the lower multi-threaded scaling and weak read-only memory bandwidth represent key performance tradeoffs. This server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, local file processing, caching layers, and lightweight database workloads that benefit from high local storage capacity and strong single-core execution.
